newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up on selective buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly higher on Tuesday due to selective buying of companies that have already issued favourable 1996 annual results, brokers said.
The index ended up 0.25 points or 0.15 percent at 159.52 on turnover of HK$90.4 million against Monday's HK$83.8 million.
"Investors are keen to buy shares in companies that have already published strong results," said an analyst at J&A Securities.
Less than half of the 44 Shenzhen-listed B share companies have made their results public ahead of the official April 30 deadline.
"The mood of the market is still depressed due to uncertainty over companies that have not published their results," the analyst said.
The A share index erased morning losses, helping to boost the B share market, brokers said.
The A share index ended 0.74 points or 0.16 percent higher to 459.83 on turnover of 7.74 billion yuan against 8.4 billion yuan on Monday.
"Investors are not really sure where the A share index is heading, so it is difficult to predict the direction of the B share market," said an analyst at a foreign investment bank.
But analysts said they expect trading in the B share market to pick up after all companies announce their annual results.
"A lot of the B share investors take long-term views and will start trading actively again once they know how the companies have performed," the analyst said.
On the B share market, Shenzhen Lionda Holdings Co Ltd was the top performer, gaining HK$0.23 or 6.39 percent to HK$3.83 on volume of 10,940 shares.
B share Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd rose HK$0.35 or 4.45 percent to HK$8.21 on volume of 1.71 million shares.
